summary: Gobber is a multi-agent AI backend for coding tasks. A FastAPI server sends each question through a LangGraph workflow that classifies it, writes Python with DeepSeek, runs the code in an isolated Docker sandbox, reviews the result, and stores approved solutions in Qdrant so similar tasks can reuse them. PostgreSQL keeps users and chat history, a Streamlit chat app is the interface, and Compose, Prometheus and Alembic cover setup and operations.

project.name: Gobber
project.summary: A FastAPI backend and Streamlit chat app for a multi-agent coding assistant. LangGraph routes each question, writes and runs Python in a locked-down Docker sandbox, reviews the result, and stores successful solutions in Qdrant; PostgreSQL keeps users and chat history.

annotations.note: The JWT signing key and token lifetime are hardcoded here; move them into settings before production.
Every valid token is treated as user 1, so all accounts share one chat history.
Prometheus instrumentation is registered twice, so the metrics middleware is installed twice.
The example settings file omits DEEPSEEK_API_KEY even though the app refuses to start without it.

flows.name: Ask the assistant
flows.title: Ask the assistant
flows.description: A chat question is classified, answered directly or turned into code that runs and is reviewed.

steps.note: A person types a question in the chat screen.
POST /api/v1/agent/ask checks the token and starts the workflow with an empty state.
The router node classifies the request and chooses a branch.
DeepSeek labels the question as general QA, research or code.
Code tasks search Qdrant for a similar solution that already passed review.
The coder writes Python using the task, the recalled solution and any feedback.
The runner posts the code to the sandbox.
The sandbox runs the file under a timeout and returns stdout and stderr.
The critic passes the output or sends feedback back to the coder, up to three tries.
An approved solution is embedded and saved for future tasks.
The screen shows the answer, or the generated code and its output.

flows.name: Start the system
flows.title: Start the system
flows.description: One script brings up the services, prepares the database and starts the API and chat app.

steps.note: ./start.sh creates and activates the virtual environment if needed.
Docker Compose starts PostgreSQL, Redis, Qdrant, the sandbox and the monitoring stack.
Alembic creates or updates the database tables.
Uvicorn serves the main API on port 8000.
Prometheus starts scraping the API's metrics.
Streamlit opens the chat screen and calls the API.

flows.name: Fix a failed run
flows.title: Fix a failed run
flows.description: A failed execution loops back to the coder with feedback until it passes or runs out of tries.

steps.note: The graph sends coding tasks down the code branch.
The coder writes the first version of the program.
The runner sends it to the sandbox.
The sandbox returns output or an error.
The critic fails the result and writes what went wrong.
The coder receives that feedback and rewrites the code.
After a pass, the working solution is saved to Qdrant.
